added_failures_note: set(after_suite.failure_ids) - set(baseline_suite.failure_ids): both arms carry tests/test_crew_recover.py::test_a_stopped_run_with_no_session_anywhere_still_reads_discardable, so the added set is empty; read from gate-base-*.log and gate-head-*.log under the reviewed run directory

reuse.reason: the attempt claim and the node-dispatch claim share only the exclusive os.open call; their claim paths, retry loops and staleness rules differ (the attempt claim re-derives its path and advances its number after a reclaim; the dispatch claim keys on holder liveness and an empty-record grace). Four plan reviews of a consolidation section each found a real interface mismatch, so a shared function would add coupling without removing logic; the consolidation section is deferred

findings.text: follow-on: assert launched["pid"] == liveness._absent_pid() compares the record against the value the test's own launcher seam returns (_resume returns {"pid": pid} straight from the seam at reckon/crew/resumption.py:1315), so it holds whenever the door returns without raising and cannot distinguish a launch from a return that never spawned; the same shape recurs at :311, though both tests retain a real guard in the raise/no-raise on the same calls.

follow-on: claim_next_attempt and _create_attempt_claim re-implement the O_CREAT|O_EXCL claim-file-with-reclaim capability the repository already owns at reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:491 (_claim_node_dispatch, with _reclaim_stale_node_dispatch_claim and _empty_claim_is_stale); the staleness predicates differ (pointer-progress versus holder-liveness) so a full merge is a refactor, but the mechanism is duplicated rather than factored, and the bounded-reclaim comment is copied near-verbatim.

follow-on: the head-arm `tests:` summary states the four chunk logs sum to "654 passed, 1 failed" where the logs themselves sum to 653 passed, 1 failed (76+384+96+97); the substantive claim is unaffected, but the quoted total does not reconcile with the logs it cites.
